prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports (keep safety authority): Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; optional Passenger Misconnect Count); these reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Gate Conflict Detector; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine: emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time); Aircraft Operator Representative (Flight Intent Messages; challenges via Decision Log); Regional Flow Manager (RFM); Slot Coordinator; Data Governance Steward (DGS); Meteorology Briefing Officer; Airport Duty Manager (ADM; Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor; System Support Engineer (SSE); Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Network Operations Liaison; Airspace Sector Planner; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance State; Contingency Fallback State (ADM declares after consulting RFM). No silent mode changes. Deployment: Readiness Gates 2-4 (interfaces, procedures, training/shadow ops/acceptance before live); interface certification separate. Expansion in waves with stabilization monitored by SSE and DGS; RFM declares full deployment. Support: SSE 24/7 on-call for Platform, Portal, SAE, DMS, Arrival Regulation Console, Alert Hub; raised posture in peaks, Adverse Weather, Capacity Reduction, Recovery (joins Digital Briefing Room); service desk business hours. SSE advises only, no traffic instructions; RFM, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, ADM, Network Operations Liaison keep command.

New part:
S923: The System Support Engineer shall maintain an incident record that captures the initial symptom, affected components, operational state, timeline, mitigation actions, data corrections, and supervisor decisions.
S924: Incident records shall reference the Audit Event Ledger where user actions, configuration changes, interface events, or automated decisions are relevant to the investigation.
S925: The Collaborative Decision Log shall be used to preserve the operational context of major incidents when traffic management decisions are made while a technical degradation is present.
S926: If the Regional Flow Platform cannot support safe collaborative operation, the Regional Flow Manager may direct transition to Contingency Fallback State using approved local procedures.
S927: The System Support Engineer shall verify that fallback tools, exported operational data, and restoration checkpoints are available before advising that normal technical service can resume.
S928: Post incident review shall be required for critical incidents, repeated high priority incidents, security related events, and failures that occur during capacity constrained operations.
S929: The review shall identify technical root cause, operational contributing factors, effectiveness of workarounds, user communication quality, and corrective actions assigned to named owners.
S930: Planned change windows shall normally be scheduled during low demand night periods and shall be coordinated with the Regional Flow Manager, Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, and affected Aircraft Operator Representative groups before approval.
S931: Changes that modify the Business Rules Registry, Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, Flight Data Exchange, or operational metering behavior shall require additional validation in a representative test environment before production release.
S932: Emergency changes may be applied outside the standard window when needed to restore service, protect cyber security, or prevent material operational harm, but they shall be documented and retrospectively approved.
S933: Service level targets shall include monthly availability for critical production functions, incident response time, restoration time, data feed timeliness, and successful completion of scheduled operational reports.
S934: Availability targets shall exclude approved maintenance windows, customer network outages outside the managed boundary, and periods when operational supervisors have directed use of contingency procedures for nontechnical reasons.
S935: Performance against service targets shall be reviewed with the Regional Flow Manager and Data Governance Steward so that service quality, operational benefit, data quality, and user confidence are managed as a single operating obligation.
S936: Future enhancement of the Regional Flow Platform should be treated as an incremental extension of the operational service rather than as a replacement of the current concept.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
